alex: Kicked off microslot probing on canary pool 3. Short summary: when we lower micro-batch interval below ~1.5ms throughput up, but p99 starts creeping up on long sequences. wondering if this is KV cache churn or kernel selection flipping under larger batches.
mira: Nice. Can you paste the quick perf snapshot? p99 numbers + kernel switch logs would help.
sam: Put a small pprof dump here from the run (trimmed). Noticed a kernel swap at ~120s into the test.
```
# pprof top (tokens/sec)
Total: 48s
  fused_attn_forward  18.2s  37.9%
  cuda_kernel_A       12.1s  25.2%  <-- appears after batch size bump
  kv_lookup           6.4s   13.3%
  scheduler_overhead  5.5s   11.5%
```
jonas: That kernel_swap looks like the optimizer choosing the large-batch kernel path. If the microbatch interval is too short we get bigger effective batches which trigger that path. The kernel has ~+10% throughput but spills more registers causing latency variance.
lia: Also saw KV miss rate jump from 2% -> 7% around the same time window. Might be that coalesce delay + deterministic timer creates alignment and evicts hot entries.
mira: Do we have queue policy config? LIFO vs FIFO could matter for tail latency and cache priming.
alex: Canary config: 
```
coalesce_delay_ms: 1.2
microslot_interval_ms: 1.0
jitter_strategy: fixed_small
queue_policy: FIFO
token_budget_target: 128
```
sam: Tried switching queue_policy -> LIFO on the next run. p99 improved ~12% but throughput dropped slightly. KV miss reduced to ~4%.
jonas: LIFO helps priming because hot requests rejoin the front and reuse KV cache. But it increases fairness problems for multi-tenant paths.
lia: We experimented with adding jitter (uniform 0-0.6ms) to break alignment. That reduced kernel swap frequency by ~60% and smoothed p99, but token-level cost increased ~1.8% due to slightly smaller batches.
mira: So tradeoffs: smaller microslot -> bigger effective batch -> kernel swap (higher variance). Add jitter -> avoid deterministic alignment -> fewer kernel swaps but less batching efficiency. Queue policy tweaks can recover cache hit rate.
alex: Actionable plan:
- Run 3x canary runs with microslot_interval_ms = [1.0, 1.4, 2.0] and jitter uniform 0-0.6ms
- For each run, toggle queue_policy FIFO/LIFO and record: throughput, p50/p95/p99, KV hit%, kernel_swap_count, token_cost
- If LIFO fixes p99 without breaking multi-tenant fairness in synthetic tenants, consider hybrid: per-route priming hint that temporarily promotes hot route to front
jonas: +1. Also add a kernel-selection guard to avoid switching to the large-batch kernel unless nvprof shows >X% sustained batch width for 10s. That buys us stability.
perf-bot: Canary jobs enqueued: run-4432109876-a, run-4432109876-b, run-4432109876-c :white_check_mark:
sam: I'll collect results and post CSV here once runs finish. Short-term tweak: prefer jittered microslot + FIFO and a conservative kernel guard.
mira: Thanks — please include a small script to reproduce microburst arrival pattern when you post results. We should ensure synthetic load triggers same KV patterns.
alex: Will do. Posting results in this thread in ~2h. :thumbsup:
